explanation: The Soviet Union took the prisoners it shot in April and May 1940 when it occupied eastern Poland in September 1939, the half the pact's secret protocol of 23 August had assigned it. Without that protocol there is no Soviet advance into Poland that autumn, and without the advance the NKVD does not hold twenty-two thousand Polish officers, policemen and officials to shoot. The type is `enabled` because the pact says nothing about what to do with prisoners. Stalin and Beria gave the order of March 1940, and the reasoning behind it belonged to Soviet policy, which was to remove the officer class of a state the two signatories had agreed to abolish. The treaty put those men in Soviet hands, and that is the sense in which it is a condition of the massacre.
